body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Blessed Noble <s>Tārā</s>.

children.translated_text: With the splendor of the crest-jewel beautiful upon the excellent heads of gods, coppery as the sight of the young sun,
whose devotion is made manifest like lac applied, composed through the touch of the wealth of passionate love not too long ago —
O Noble One, with devotion I [bow to] your feet, my head bent down by the weight of the crown formed by my cupped hands,
O Savioress, I worship [you] with garlands of fresh <s>nuta</s> flowers, [you who are] the supreme refuge. (verse 1)
Having fallen bodily into the impassable fire of suffering, wretched, looking in all directions,

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ mūḍhaḥ karomīty asakṛd api kṛtārambhavaiyarthyakhinnaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What, what shall I, the deluded one, do?' — thus distressed by the repeated futility of [my] undertakings,

children.text: śrutvā bhūyaḥ parebhyaḥ kṣatanayana iva vyomni candrārkalakṣmīm
children.translated_text: Hearing again from others, like one with injured eyes [hearing of] the beauty of the moon and sun in the sky,

children.text: ālokāśānibaddhaḥ paragatigamanas tvāṃ śraye pāpahantrīṃ // Tss_2
children.translated_text: My hopes fixed on the light, one who goes by the path of others — I take refuge in you, O destroyer of sins. (verse 2)

children.text: sarvasmin satvamārge nanu tava karuṇā nirviśeṣaṃ pravṛttā
children.translated_text: Surely your compassion extends without distinction upon the entire path of beings,

children.text: tanmadhye tadgraheṇa grahaṇam upagataṃ mādṛśasyāpy avaśyam /
children.translated_text: And within that [scope], the apprehension of one such as me through the grasp of that [compassion] is inevitable.
And [your] unparalleled power is the orb of the fierce-rayed [sun] to the darkness of the sins of the entire world —

children.text: duḥkhīvāhaṃ tathāpi pratapati dhig aho duṣkṛtaṃ durvidagdham // Tss_3
children.translated_text: Yet even so, I who am suffering still burn. Alas, shame! How wicked and ill-fated is [my] evil deed! (verse 3)

children.text: dhig dhig māṃ mandabhāgyaṃ divasakararucāpy apraṇuṇṇāndhakāraṃ
children.translated_text: Shame, shame on me, the unfortunate one, whose darkness is not dispelled even by the radiance of the sun,
Who thirsts at the very bank of the <s>Haimavatī</s> (Ganges), cool with fragments of snow and stone,
Who is destitute within the jewel-island's broad avenue, in the interior of houses that are caves of great gems,

children.text: nāthīkṛtvāpy ānāthaṃ bhagavati bhavatīṃ sarvalokaikadhātrīm // Tss_4
children.translated_text: Who, though having made you his protectress, O Blessed One, remains without a protector — you who are the sole sustainer of all the worlds. (verse 4)

children.text: mātāpi stanyahetor viruvati bahuśaḥ khedam āyāti putre
children.translated_text: Even a mother, when her child cries repeatedly for milk, becomes weary and distressed;

children.text: krodhaṃ dhatte pitāpi pratidivasam asatprārthanāsu prayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even a father grows angry when constantly engaged with his son's improper requests.
But you are the foremost vine upon the great wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>) yielding the abundant fruit of the desires of the three worlds,

children.text: sarvebhyo 'bhyārcitārthān visṛjasi na ca te vikriyā jātu kācit // Tss_5
children.translated_text: You bestow upon all their desired objects of worship, and yet no alteration whatsoever ever arises in you. (verse 5)

children.text: yo yaḥ kleśoghavahnijvalitatanur ahaṃ tāraṇī tasya tasye-
children.translated_text: 'Whoever burns with body aflame in the fire of the mass of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) — I am that one's savioress' —

children.text: tyātmopajñāṃ pratijñāṃ kuru mayi saphalāṃ duḥkhapātālamagne /
children.translated_text: Make this self-proclaimed vow of yours fruitful in me, who am plunged in the abyss of suffering!

children.text: vardhante yāvad ante paruṣaparibhavāḥ prāṇināṃ duḥkhavegāḥ
children.translated_text: For as long as the harsh insults and surges of suffering of beings increase at the end,
Just so long does the compassion of those whose minds are sustained by resolve (<s>praṇidhi</s>) on the path of perfect enlightenment (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) [increase]. (verse 6)

children.text: ity uccair ūrdhvabāhau nadati nutipadavyājam ākrandanādaṃ
children.translated_text: When thus, with arms raised high, one cries out a lament in the guise of a hymn of praise,

children.text: nārhaty anyo 'py upekṣāṃ janani janayituṃ kiṃ punar yādṛśī tvam /
children.translated_text: Not even another is justified in showing indifference, O Mother — how much less one such as you!
Seeing that others' prayers for desired wealth are fulfilled by you,

children.text: dahye sahyena bhūyastaram aratibhuvā saṃtatāntarjvareṇa // Tss_7
children.translated_text: I burn all the more with an unbearable, unceasing inner fever — a dwelling-place of displeasure. (verse 7)

children.text: pāpī yady asmi kasmāt tvayi mama mahatī vardhate bhaktir eṣā
children.translated_text: If I am a sinner, then why does this great devotion to you increase in me?

children.text: śrutyā smṛtyā ca nāmno 'py apaharasi haṭhāt pāpam ekā tvam eva /
children.translated_text: By the mere hearing and remembering of [your] name, you alone forcibly remove sin.

children.text: tyaktavyāpārabhārā nudasi mayi kathaṃ kathyatāṃ tathyakathye
children.translated_text: How then do you push me aside, having abandoned the burden of [your] activity? Let the truth be told in truthful speech:

children.text: pathyaṃ glāne mariṣyaty api vipulakṛpaḥ kiṃ bhiṣag rorudhīti // Tss_8
children.translated_text: Does a greatly compassionate physician withhold medicine from a sick man who is about to die, saying 'Let him be restrained'? (verse 8)
Assailed simultaneously and progressively by base [foes] such as illusion (<s>māyā</s>), jealousy (<s>mātsarya</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and the like,
And by one's own faults — like a young camel in a stable, [burdened] with loads belonging to many —

children.text: yuṣmatpādābjapūjāṃ kṣaṇam api na labhe yat tadarthaṃ viśeṣād
children.translated_text: I do not obtain even a moment for the worship of your lotus feet; for that very purpose, especially,
May this composition of words and syllables, humble with wretchedness, be one whose desire is not barren for me. (verse 9)
From the ocean whose playful surging waves, tossing and rolling, are churned by the wind whirling at the end of an aeon,
whose turbulent upheaval casts up the shore-terraces with the violent cracking and shattering — with roaring laughter,
By those whose ships are shattered and who are sinking, faint and still with pitiful weeping and wailing,

children.text: svacchandaṃ devi sadyas tvadabhibhūtiparais tīram uttīryate 'bdheḥ // Tss_10
children.translated_text: O Goddess, the shore of the ocean is freely crossed at once by those who are intent on your sovereignty. (verse 10)
Those whose beds rest in houses whose rooms are bright with the swift blazing of flames, fiercely flaring,
with sparks creeping in the interior of the sky-house born from the womb of clouds bewildered by smoke,
With hands joined in salutation to you, crowns [bowed], their prayers uttered in stammering tones,
Are sprinkled in an instant by [streams] swift as freshly-arising clouds brilliant with the play of lightning. (verse 11)
Of an elephant whose hanging garland-rows cling to the rims of both cheeks overflowing with the waters of rut,
whose fire of hatred is born from the rival elephant summoned by the '<s>huṃ</s>'-roar,
[A person] whose body is tossed upon the high swing-platform at the tips of [its] tusks, having remembered you, defies death,
Delighted, seated upon the peak-crest of a broad mountain-summit. (verse 12)
In the festival of the pike-thrusting vine of spears impaled upon severed human heads,
In the desolate wilderness, bandits whose swelling pride bursts forth from the sword gleaming at their fingertips,
whose eyes dart with sidelong glances beneath brows crooked with furrowed scowls — [she] yokes them into servitude;
The stylus of [your] thought, inscribing clearly and tirelessly the words that are the abode of your name's glory. (verse 13)
The lion, having split open with the edge of his terrible diamond-hard blows the frontal globes of maddened elephants,
his shoulder-joints thick with matted manes, fearsome and bristling, washed by streams of dense blood flowing [from them],

children.text: krudhyann āpitsur ārād upari mṛgaripus tīkṣṇadāṃṣṭrotkaṭāsyas
children.translated_text: raging, rushing from afar from above, the enemy of deer, his mouth gaping with sharp terrible fangs —
[Even he] flees in terror, turning away, [upon hearing] the words of the milk-like meaning of the hymn composed in your honor. (verse 14)
With nooses of death fashioned from the ropes of flickering terrible tongues flashing from gaping mouths
engaged in the activity of hissing with the full force of the striking, spreading hoods of serpents, whose forms are distorted in the darkness of swirling smoke —

children.text: pāpāt saṃbhūya bhūyas tava guṇagaṇanā tatparas tvatparātmā
children.translated_text: [Even these], when one who is devoted to you and whose self is fixed upon you, having arisen from sin, again enumerates the host of your virtues,
he attains the splendor of a garland of blue lotuses encircled by rows of intoxicated bees as his ornament. (verse 15)
His hair roughly seized and dragged by the fierce soldiers of the battalion, terrified by the furrowing of the master's brow,
bound tightly by the knots of harsh ropes amidst the loud rattling shouts of agitated, sharp-tongued servants,

children.text: kṣuttṛṭkṣāmoṣṭhakaṇṭhas tyajati sa sapadi vyāpadaṃ tāṃ durantāṃ
children.translated_text: [even such a one] instantly abandons that endless calamity — hunger and thirst parching his lips and throat —
whoever takes refuge at the feet of the noble <s>Tārā</s>, even though abandoned by his affectionate kinsmen. (verse 16)
The <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), [with] their illusory attacks employing the sequence of magical creative acts, manifold false costumes and disguises,
and the dazzle and tumult of weapons and rays befitting [those] assumed forms —
they bear an inviolable protection for one whose sins are removed by the recollection of the <s>mantra</s> extracted from your <s>tantra</s>,
[those <s>rākṣasas</s>] strung with rows of the gut-string instruments made from the entrails strung upon corpses. (verse 17)
In the darkness of bound torrents from the three-fold rut-fluid river of [war-elephants] whose forms are like roaring thunderclouds,
with weapon-rays gleaming like lightning-flashes, amid a shower of falling arrows,
one who is hemmed in during the time of battle by enemies and foes of mighty arm-strength,

children.text: tvaddattotsāhapuṣṭiḥ prasabham arimahīm ekavīraḥ pinaṣṭi // Tss_18
children.translated_text: nourished with the courage bestowed by you, he alone, a single hero, crushes the enemy's land by force. (verse 18)
Those whose limbs are wounded and devoured by creatures issuing from the cavity-mouths of the veins attached to the skin and flesh,
foul-smelling with putrid pus and blood flowing from the disease that has arisen and increased through the continuation of sinful conduct —
devoted through the practice of the supreme pill-remedy that is the service of your feet,
they become persons with bodies resembling refined gold, with eyes wide as lotuses. (verse 19)

children.text: viśrāntaṃ śrotrapātre gurubhir upahṛtāṃ yāsya nāmnāyaṃ bhaikṣyaṃ
children.translated_text: One whose begged alms, offered by elders, have come to rest in the bowl of his ear [i.e., who has heard teachings],

children.text: vidvadgoṣṭhīṣu yaś ca śrutadhanavirahān mūkatām abhyupaiti /
children.translated_text: and who yet lapses into muteness in the assemblies of the learned, bereft of the wealth of learning,
having attained the lordship of speech, adorned with the splendor of all ornamental [figures of speech],

children.text: so 'pi tvadbhaktiśaktyā harati nṛpasabhe vādisiṃhāsanāni // Tss_20
children.translated_text: even he, by the power of devotion to you, seizes the thrones of debaters in the king's assembly. (verse 20)
His body exposed through the tearing of rags, his joints stiff, dusty and grimy from sleeping on the ground,
crushing lice with his nails, standing before others' houses with a begging-bowl, seeking sustenance,
having worshipped you and exerted himself, [he wins] a beautiful queen fanned with waving <s>cāmara</s> whisks, smiling,
and rules the earth, dense with the tusks of intoxicated elephants, under a single raised parasol. (verse 21)
Those who are wearied by the successive means of service, craft-work, ingenuity, exchange, and gift-giving,
not obtaining wealth — the auspicious fruit accumulated from merit acquired in previous births,

children.text: daivātikrāmanīṃ tvāṃ kṛpaṇajanajanany artham abhyarthya bhūyo
children.translated_text: having entreated you, O mother of the wretched, who surpass even fate, for wealth, again
the destitute obtain treasures of heaps of pure gold from the earth. (verse 22)
Embarrassed when his livelihood is cut off, reproached by his wife in her tattered garments,
shunned from afar by his own people, sons, friends, and relatives because of his self-centeredness,
having disclosed his suffering to you, [he becomes lord] of houses whose boundaries are dug up by horse-hooves,
and rules, awakened from sleep by the tinkling of the bangles of the women of his own inner chambers. (verse 23)
A wheel [of sovereignty] touching the circles of the directions, with brilliant spreading rays, a woman endowed with [auspicious] marks as ornaments,
a six-tusked chief elephant, a fine horse with dark hair beautiful as a peacock's neck,
a gem radiant with blazing lustrous rays, a treasurer of flawless qualities, possessing a full treasury,

children.text: senānīr vīrasainyo bhavati bhagavati tvatprasādāṃśaleśāt // Tss_24
children.translated_text: a commander with a heroic army — [all these] come into being from even a fraction of your grace, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>. (verse 24)
Self-willed, [dwelling] in a beautiful chamber appointed with fragrant sandalwood-water and gem-stone slabs,
with genuine hospitality freshly arranged out of love for amorous play with his beloved,
having attained <s>siddhi</s> (supernatural power) through your <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), a lord of <s>Vidyādharas</s> goes to the <s>Malaya</s> sandal-forest,
with massive raised arms [strong as] iron bars, darkened by the gleam of his sword, with flashing <s>pārihārya</s> (armlets). (verse 25)
With breasts covered by necklaces, with wide eyes rivaling the blue lotuses at their ears,
With bees irresistibly intoxicated by the fresh fragrance of their generous braids adorned with <s>Mandāra</s> flowers,
With beautiful ankle-bell music following the sound of their waist-chains, their feet raised ever higher—

children.text: tvannāthaṃ prārthayante smaramadamuditāḥ sādarā devakanyāḥ // Tss_26
children.translated_text: Divine maidens, delighted with the intoxication of <s>Smara</s> (love), respectfully court your lord. (verse 26)
With pools concealed within, [bearing] garlands of golden lotuses with diamond filaments,
With canopies of pollen shaken by the sweet honey of emerging <s>Pārijāta</s> trees,
With sweet music provided by celestial city ladies skilled in <s>vīṇā</s> and flute—
Having performed your worship, one enjoys for long the excursion to the <s>Nandana</s> garden. (verse 27)
In [the river] whose water is fragrant with camphor, cardamom, clove bark, <s>agaru</s>, and <s>nalada</s>,
Whose waves rest in the whirlpool-like recesses of the proud, prominent breasts of subdued [beauties],
In the <s>Mandākinī</s>, with beautiful women playing in its abundantly splashing waters—
Those whose power of merit has fully ripened through hearts devoted to you play [there]. (verse 28)
Whose commands are honored by the leaders of the gods with heads bowed deeply in reverence,
Seated firmly in the lap of heaven, upon the divine elephant whose body gleams with jingling ornaments,
His body covered with abundant horripilation from being swung on the rope-swing of <s>Śacī</s>'s arms—

children.text: pūtas tvaddṛṣṭipātair avati suramahīṃ hīrabhinnaprakoṣṭhaḥ // Tss_29
children.translated_text: Purified by the falling of your gaze, with forearms adorned with diamond [bracelets], he protects the divine realm. (verse 29)
With a canopy of the sky-splendor of <s>Sugatas</s> seated on thrones adorned with crest-jewel ornaments,
Filling the three worlds with rays sharper than millions of rising young suns,
With one foot in the mature <s>ālīḍha</s> posture, before which <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> bow under the weight of your steps—

children.text: tvadrūpaṃ bhāvyamānaṃ bhavati bhavabhayocchittaye janmabhājām // Tss_30
children.translated_text: Your form, when meditated upon, becomes the destroyer of the fear of existence for those who have taken birth. (verse 30)
Some see [your form as] wrathful, with arm-branches swirling with rays of weapons,
Pervading the expanse of the sky, with terrible conduct adorned by serpent-hood bracelets,
With frightening laughter that terrifies enemies, with the <s>ḍamaru</s> drum of the <s>Ḍāmara</s> rite, with the beating of the <s>ḍāmara</s>—
Fierce with the tumult of the great sport of intoxicated delight with the rhythm of rising <s>vetālas</s>. (verse 31)
But some [see you] as having, in the expanse of sky entered through each rising hair-pore, upon each level of earth,
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s> and other beings — humans, wind-gods, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s> — established,
Adorned with the wonderful emanations of hundreds of <s>Sugatas</s> established with splendor pervading the circle of directions—
Wondrous, worshipped by the three worlds, having the nature of all beings composed of the moving and the still. (verse 32)
Some [see it as] red like the sun with rays reddened by the color of lac and <s>sindūra</s>;
Others [see it as] blue like the powder ground from glorious dense sapphire leaves;
Some [see it as] whiter than the churned milk of the ocean of milk, and some as golden—

children.text: tvadrūpaṃ viśvarūpaṃ sphaṭikavad upadhāyuktibhedād vibhinnam // Tss_33
children.translated_text: Your form is the universal form, appearing differently like crystal according to differences in the method of approach. (verse 33)
The sole witness of all knowable realities revealed by the lamp of omniscient knowledge

children.text: sākṣād vetti tvadīyaṃ guṇagaṇagaṇanāṃ sarvavit tatsuto vā /
children.translated_text: Directly knows the enumeration of the multitudes of your qualities — the all-knowing one or his son.

children.text: yat tu vyādāya vaktraṃ valibhujaraṭitaṃ mādṛśo raṭīti
children.translated_text: But that one like me opens his wrinkled, wizened mouth and babbles—
That effort, born from the pain of the fever of intense suffering, is a cause for laughter. (verse 34)

children.text: yan me vijñapsyamānaṃ prathamataram adas tvaṃ viśeṣeṇa vettrī
children.translated_text: What I am about to express, you already know first and foremost, O especially discerning one;
The effort of speaking beyond [your knowledge] is a cause of satisfaction for the foolish heart.

children.text: kiṃ tu snigdhasya bandhor viṣaṃ iva purato duḥkham udgīrya vācā
children.translated_text: But like vomiting poison before a loving friend, having poured forth suffering in words,

children.text: jñātārthasyāpi duḥkhī hṛdayalaghutayā svasthatāṃ vindatīva // Tss_35
children.translated_text: Even the sufferer who knows the matter finds well-being, as it were, through the lightening of the heart. (verse 35)
O crescent moon manifest in the ocean of auspicious bliss, bestow your cool gaze!

children.text: puṣṭiṃ jñānopadeśaiḥ kuru ghanakaruṇe dhvaṃsaya dhvāntamantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nourish [me] with teachings of knowledge, O deeply compassionate one; destroy the inner darkness!
In me, whose mind is purified by the waters of your hymn, [may there be] the sole abode of welfare,

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ yasmād amoghaṃ jagati tava guṇastotramātraṃ prajānām // Tss_36
children.translated_text: For it is seen that the mere hymn of your qualities is never fruitless for beings in the world. (verse 36)

children.text: saṃstutya tvadguṇaughāvayavam aniyateyattam āptaṃ mayā yat /
children.translated_text: Having praised even a portion of the flood of your qualities, of unlimited extent, whatever merit has been obtained by me,
That merit, whose sweet taste is the fruit of the desire for auspicious days, is to be enjoyed until liberation—
By that merit, may the world proceed to that land marked with the auspicious <s>svastika</s> signs on the soles of noble <s>Lokeśvara</s>'s feet,

children.text: ahnāyāyaṃ prayāyāt sugatasutamahīṃ tāṃ sukhāvatyupākhyām // Tss_37
children.translated_text: Day by day, to that land of the son of the <s>Sugata</s>, called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Blissful). (verse 37)
